title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 206: Nature's Sticky Secret: The Science of Dry Adhesion
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 206 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Nature's Sticky Secret: The Science of Dry Adhesion

Paragraph 1. For over two thousand years, scientists wondered how geckos climb so easily. A gecko is a small lizard that can run fast up walls and across smooth glass ceilings. Tree frogs need wet liquid on their feet to stick, and insects use tiny sharp claws. However, the gecko walks on ceilings without glue or claws, and its feet leave no dirty marks behind. Only in the twenty-first century did powerful microscopes finally show how gecko feet work.

Paragraph 2. A gecko's foot does not use sticky liquid; it uses pure physical contact. Under a strong microscope, each gecko toe has millions of tiny hairs, much thinner than one human hair. Every tiny hair splits into hundreds of even smaller flat ends. When these billions of flat ends press close to a wall, tiny forces pull the foot and wall together. Together, these tiny forces are strong enough to hold fifty times the lizard's weight.

Paragraph 3. Still, sticking tightly to a wall would be dangerous if the gecko could not move. An animal stuck forever would soon starve! Engineer Dr. Ronald Fearing explains that gecko feet depend on direction. When a gecko pulls its foot down and in, the tiny hairs stick strongly to the wall. When the gecko rolls its toes upward, the hairs change angle and let go right away. That is why geckos can run over one metre per second up walls.

Paragraph 4. Scientists wanted to copy gecko feet to make new dry tape. Early plastic tapes failed fast because the artificial hairs stuck together when pressed. Later, Dr. Kellar Autumn used super-small carbon tubes to build much stronger dry tape. Today, doctors test gecko tape to close cuts inside the body without stitches, and engineers build robot hands for space to catch old broken satellites.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...walks on ceilings without glue or claws..."
Đoạn 2: "...each gecko toe has millions of tiny hairs..."
Đoạn 3: "When the gecko rolls its toes upward, the hairs change angle and let go..."
Đoạn 4: "...build robot hands for space to catch old broken satellites."

q5.text: Tree frogs use dry hairs on their feet to climb wet surfaces.

steps: Đoạn 1: Ếch cây cần chất lỏng ướt (wet liquid), không phải lông khô.

q6.text: A gecko's feet can support up to fifty times its own body weight.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...strong enough to hold fifty times the lizard's weight."

q7.text: Early plastic gecko tapes worked well under heavy pressure.

steps: Đoạn 4: Băng dính nhựa đời đầu hỏng nhanh (failed fast) khi bị đè ép.

q8.text: Dr. Kellar Autumn spent twenty years studying geckos in Asian forests.

steps: Đoạn 4: Bài không nhắc thời gian hay việc ông nghiên cứu ở rừng châu Á.
